title: assess-split-backward-schedule
summary: Evaluate memory-capped split-backward and V-shaped pipeline scheduling proposals, preserving synchronous update, global-batch and optimizer-validation semantics.

skill_metadata.name: assess-split-backward-schedule
skill_metadata.description: Evaluate memory-capped split-backward and V-shaped pipeline scheduling proposals, preserving synchronous update, global-batch and optimizer-validation semantics.

applicability.scope: Assessing memory-capped split-backward and V-shaped pipeline schedule proposals when a pipeline trace suggests input-gradient propagation waits behind deferrable weight-gradient work or an optimizer barrier, while preserving synchronous update, global-batch and optimizer-validation semantics
applicability.prerequisites: The packaged evidence notes are read before citing the paper; installing or running frameworks, benchmarking schedules, changing training semantics, configuring hardware or modifying repositories needs separate authorization
applicability.input_contract: Stage and microbatch counts, microbatch and global batch, precision, optimizer and clipping/NaN behavior; F, input-gradient B, weight-gradient W and transfer timings; per-pass retained and released bytes; total device peak and margin; collective ordering; kernel-splitting support; calculated bubble rate kept apart from measured idle time and useful samples/s
applicability.produced_artifact: A candidate schedule and fallback with per-pass order rationale, peak-memory and transfer costs, unchanged semantic requirements, counter-signals and a future verification proposal; a reviewable plan, not an enabled schedule
failure_modes: Completion of B is equated with releasing all activations, so W inputs retained by deferral go uncounted
The equal-time zero-bubble construction replaces observed F/B/W and transfer times, or kernel-splitting and synchronization overhead is left out
The schedule is chosen by minimum modeled bubble rate instead of whole-step throughput under the memory and quality constraint
pMB activation capacity is read as total memory, hiding HBM, workspace, buffers or per-rank imbalance
Removing the optimizer barrier drops global norm, clipping or NaN decisions, rollback and re-update, or the correctness of work that depends on a tentative update
Optimizer post-validation is conflated with accepting stale-gradient delayed updates
applicability.refusal_point: Withholds an enablement recommendation under frequent clipping/NaNs, small available memory, strongly unequal passes, unsupported split kernels, hidden collectives or dynamic shapes, and retains the synchronized fallback while optimizer reversibility and rollback coverage are unverified

recommendations: Compare ordinary 1F1B with a memory-capped split schedule first; add V-shaped two-chunk placement only when memory permits, and at matched global batch also try smaller microbatches with more microbatches.
Decide optimizer post-validation separately from the schedule change.
In a later authorized comparison, hold model, global batch and precision fixed and compare real with calculated idle intervals.
limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
